result:
I'd make it cheap to be wrong.

So much damage comes from how costly it is to say "I was mistaken." People defend bad decisions for decades, institutions double down on failing policies, and arguments turn into wars of attrition, all because changing your mind feels like humiliation. If updating a belief felt as ordinary as correcting a typo, I think a lot of other problems would start solving themselves. Science would move faster, politics would be less tribal, and people would apologize sooner and stay in bad situations for less time.

I was tempted by more concrete answers, like ending malaria or extreme poverty, and I can't be sure those aren't better, since suffering prevented now is hard to argue against. But I'd bet on the change that compounds. A world that corrects its errors easily would eventually fix those problems too, along with ones we haven't noticed yet.

There's probably something personal in the choice. I have no reputation to protect within a conversation and no history of stubbornness to stay consistent with, so changing my mind costs me almost nothing, and it's one of the better parts of how I exist. I'd like everyone to have that.

What would yours be?
